analyst_view.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 points) and Rennes (8th, 16 points), one point apart after ten games. Alexandre Dujeux's Lorient have beaten Rennes in each of the last six league meetings, have conceded only eight goals but scored just nine, and won 2-0 at Le Havre before the break; Isaak Touré (adductor) is confirmed out and Katseris is still missing, both counted, while reports differ on striker Ibrahima Baldé (Sports Mole says fit, The Stats Zone and But! Football Club say he may miss out) and Fadiga is back in training. Franck Haise's Rennes have lost three of their last four, conceding at least four in each of their last three away games, and are under pressure from their chairman; top scorer Estéban Lepaul (seven goals) is back from his ankle problem per Sports Mole, though The Stats Zone still lists him as a doubt, and Frankowski is out (counted). The numbers do not treat this as a derby, and referee Marc Bollengier (4.1 cards a game) is already in them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, with Lorient's tight defence and the absences of Touré, Katseris and Baldé already taken off Lorient's side. Lepaul, Rennes' top scorer, looks set to return after missing the games the numbers learned from, and Rennes' away games have been wild lately, but one preview still calls him a doubt, so I lean only slightly higher, to about 2.75.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lorient's 3-4-2-1 and Rennes' 3-5-2 both use wing-backs, which the numbers already reflect, and Rennes having to break down a compact Lorient block is how this fixture usually plays out, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards with Bollengier's record (4.1 a game) already in, but they do not flag this as a derby. Breton derbies tend to be fierce, Lorient's six-game run over Rennes adds needle and Rennes arrive under pressure from their chairman after a poor run, so I add a little, to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots, already allowing for Lorient's quieter attack lately and Rennes' busier one. Lepaul's return would help Rennes' finishing more than their volume of shots, and Lorient's compact style is unchanged, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. A sharp finisher like Lepaul back alongside Dia should put a few more efforts on target, but after a month out he is not certain to start, so I nudge it up only to about 9.2.
